pages.title: Google Search's guidance about AI-generated content

claims.claim: Using automation, including AI, to generate content with the primary purpose of manipulating search rankings is a violation of Google's spam policies.
claims.quote: to generate content with the primary purpose of manipulating ranking in search results is a violation of our spam policies.
claims.reason: Spam policies: scaled content abuse is pages generated 'for the primary purpose of manipulating search rankings', e.g. via generative AI tools.

claims.claim: Appropriate use of AI or automation is not against Google's guidelines; not all use of automation, including AI generation, is spam.
claims.quote: Appropriate use of AI or automation is not against our guidelines.
claims.reason: Guidance (2026-10-01): gen AI 'can be particularly useful'; only generating many pages without adding value may violate the scaled content abuse policy.

claims.claim: Using AI gives content no special ranking gains; content that is useful, helpful, original and satisfies aspects of E-E-A-T might do well in Search.
claims.quote: Using AI doesn't give content any special gains. It's just content.
claims.reason: Google FAQ: 'Using AI doesn't give content any special gains. It's just content.' The current guidance page still links this FAQ.

claims.claim: Google uses a variety of systems, including SpamBrain, that analyze patterns and signals to identify spam content however it is produced.
claims.quote: We have a variety of systems, including SpamBrain, that analyze patterns and signals to help us identify spam content, however it is produced.
claims.reason: Ranking systems guide: Google employs spam detection systems 'including SpamBrain' to deal with content that violates its spam policies.

claims.claim: Google says AI disclosures are useful where readers might ask how content was created, and that giving AI an author byline is probably not the best approach.
claims.quote: Giving AI an author byline is probably not the best way to follow our recommendation to make clear to readers when AI is part of the content creation process.
claims.reason: Helpful content page: 'AI or automation disclosures are useful for content where someone might think "How was this created?"'

pages.title: Does Google Penalize AI Content? An SEO Study (2026)

claims.claim: Google does not penalize AI content under its own policies.
claims.quote: Google does not penalize AI content under its own policies.
claims.reason: Google: 'Appropriate use of AI or automation is not against our guidelines'; only use primarily to manipulate rankings violates spam policies.

claims.claim: Google has applied manual actions to spammy AI-generated content, and there is evidence its algorithms can detect low-quality machine-written text.
claims.quote: Google has applied manual actions to spammy AI-generated content, and there is evidence its algorithms can detect low-quality machine-written text.
claims.reason: Google lists manual actions for scaled content abuse 'no matter how it's created', but never says it detects machine-written text. Page cites only anecdotes.

claims.claim: Rankability scored 487 top-ranking Google results with its in-house AI detector and found 83% of the pages it could score read as human-written.
claims.quote: 83% of Top Google Search Results Are Not Using AI-Generated Content
claims.reason: First-party study, no data published. A Nov 2025 copy gave the same 487 and 83% figures from Originality.ai, not the 2026 in-house detector run claimed.

claims.claim: Google says using automation, including AI, mainly to manipulate rankings violates its spam policies, but not all use of automation, including AI generation, is spam.
claims.quote: not all use of automation, including AI generation, is spam. Automation has long been used to generate helpful content, such as sports scores, weather forecasts, and transcripts.
claims.reason: Exact match to Google's Feb 2023 post: 'not all use of automation, including AI generation, is spam. Automation has long been used...'

claims.claim: Google's algorithm includes a "Helpful Content System" designed to reward high-quality content and punish the opposite.
claims.quote: This system is designed to reward high-quality content and punish the opposite.
claims.reason: Google: the helpful content system 'evolved and became part of our core ranking systems' in March 2024. Now listed under retired systems, not standalone.
